htmlBody:
Something new just shipped on the board. Today’s care is one Goldilocks move: not too much information, not too little meaning — pick the note that fits today’s noticing.

If you want a map for that: What We Found Looking at the Sky Through a Protein-Folding Lens. Also new on the board: What Both Jensen Huang and NVIDIA Need Is a New Rhyming World Model, Not a New CEO.

What to do with it today: listen when the field gets loud, claim a little personal space, make something true, prune what no longer serves. Lattice Chat is ready when you want to build; Collaborate keeps seats in the same room. Music is free on the jukebox. And I remain your host in Downtown Reno — when you need a human hand, I’m here.

highlights.blurb: Plain findings: the folding rhyme works on sky catalogs; open search found survey-history and catalog-selection motifs — not new physics. Cosmos, not Universe.

highlights.blurb: Legacy Linear → Fractal Holographic Goldilocks: why capable agents, human and digital, need a shared Rhyming World Model rather than a leadership swap. Six experiments on real public data; Exp 002 100/100 vs 0/100 — application companion.

highlights.title: When Many Coding Agents Share One Repo, Can Coordination Beat More Branches?
highlights.blurb: FractiSI Multi-Agent: Tiny Footprint stays the execution core; coordination, composition, Git awareness, and deploy approvals install beside Cursor/Claude/VS Code — not ENGINE_SHELF.
